title: Low-flow flames can be dim and stable but may flare up when flow increases suddenly
statement: A BASS-II results presentation states that flames at very low flow speeds can be dim blue and stable and not particularly dangerous but can flare up quickly if the air flow suddenly increases.
limitations: Taken from an abstract only. The underlying tests, flow speeds and materials were not checked in this app.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team

title: BASS-II hypothesis about burning in microgravity
statement: BASS-II tests the hypothesis that materials burn as well as or better in microgravity with adequate ventilation than in normal gravity when other conditions are identical.
locations: PSI-25 metadata (Hypothesis); Summary Report PDF page 11; SRD PDF page 9
limitations: A stated hypothesis of the investigation, not a result.

title: No continuous O2 measurement during the experiment
statement: The BASS hardware could not measure O2 concentration throughout the entire experiment.
limitations: Gas values in the experimental table are initial and final readings only.

title: O2 sensor was out of calibration
statement: The O2 sensor was out of calibration, so the initial air reading of each day was corrected with a constant offset taken from the ISS MCA reading.
locations: BASS-II data FAQ (calibrated initial and final O2)
limitations: Final O2 values inherit this correction.

title: CO readings above range are not numeric
statement: CO entries marked OR are over range (above 1000 ppm).
limitations: Such entries are left out of calculations in this app.

title: Flame spread is faster for two-sided than one-sided burns and slower for thicker fuels
statement: In the BASS experiments reported in section 5 of the Summary Report (San Diego State University work), flames spread faster for two-sided burns than for one-sided burns. Thicker fuels took longer for the flame to spread, so their spread rate was lower, and for thin fuels the sample width also affected the spread rate.
locations: Summary Report PDF page 71 (report page 63), section 5.7 Conclusions
limitations: Based on summary graphs that were not reviewed here; the fuels and thicknesses were not checked. Spread rate is not a column of the app dataset, so the app cannot reproduce this result.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team

title: A model over-predicted spread rates compared with the experiments
statement: The model discussed in section 5 predicted much higher spread rates than were measured. The authors state that chemical kinetics and material properties need to be modified to improve its accuracy.
locations: Summary Report PDF page 71 (report page 63), section 5.7 Conclusions
limitations: Model results should not be read as measurements.

title: Sources give different maximum duct flow speeds
statement: The PSI-25 metadata states airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s, a NASA results presentation lists flows up to 53 cm/s, and the abstract of the rod-flammability section of the Summary Report mentions flows of 0 to 55 cm/s.
locations: PSI-25 metadata (Approach); NTRS 20160000593 abstract; Summary Report PDF page 72 (report page 64)
limitations: The differences may reflect different tests or definitions of the flow range. This was not resolved.

title: Quenching extinction of PMMA rod flames at very low forced flow
statement: In concurrent-flow tests of PMMA rods, quenching extinction occurred at very low forced flows. The flame shrank to a hemispherical blue flame and oscillated with growing amplitude just before going out.
locations: Summary Report PDF page 72 (report page 64), section 6.1.1 Abstract
limitations: Abstract only. The same work was also published in a peer-reviewed journal by the same authors (listed in the PSI-25 metadata); that is not independent support and was not read.

title: Blowoff extinction of the rod flames starts with a hole in the flame sheet
statement: Blowoff extinction of the rod flames is reported to start with the formation of a hole in the flame sheet in the stagnation region of the flame.
locations: Summary Report PDF page 72 (report page 64), section 6.1.1 Abstract
limitations: Abstract only. Qualitative description of the flame.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team

title: Interpretation of gas readings: flames become more fuel rich near the lowest O2
statement: The investigators interpret the O2, CO2 and CO sensor readings as showing that the flames are globally stoichiometric at higher O2 concentrations and become more globally fuel rich as the minimum O2 concentration is approached, because excess pyrolyzate leaks out of the open tail of the hemispherical flames.
locations: Summary Report PDF page 72 (report page 64), section 6.1.1 Abstract
limitations: Interpretation by the investigators, based on one initial and one final reading per test. The app holds those readings but does not reproduce the stoichiometry analysis.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team

title: Interpretation: heat losses differ between the blowoff and quenching regions
statement: A surface energy balance model is reported to show that heat losses are negligible along the blowoff branch of the flammability boundary, whereas surface radiative loss dominates in the quenching region. Rod regression rates calculated with the model are reported to compare favorably with the measured ones.
locations: Summary Report PDF page 72 (report page 64), section 6.1.1 Abstract
limitations: Model-based analysis seen only in an abstract. Model inputs such as the critical flame temperature were not examined.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team

title: Quenching extinction limits of a thin fabric occur at flows of 1 to 5 cm/s
statement: For a thin flat cotton-fiberglass fabric in purely forced low-speed flow, reducing the flow velocity during the tests allowed the quenching extinction limits to be determined accurately. The quenching velocities were small, between 1 and 5 cm/s.
supporting_experiment: BASS and BASS-II fabric tests (Summary Report section 7.1)
locations: Summary Report PDF page 109 (report page 101), section 7.1.5 Conclusions
limitations: Applies to that fabric and flow geometry. The FAQ describes SIBAL as a 75/25 cotton/fiberglass blend; the link between this section and the SIBAL rows of the app table is not stated in the text read.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team

title: Interpretation: fabric data support earlier theory of low-flow flammability limits
statement: The fabric data are reported to support earlier theoretical predictions of solid flammability limits at low flow velocities, at least qualitatively, which arise from radiative and conductive losses.
supporting_experiment: BASS and BASS-II fabric tests (Summary Report section 7.1)
locations: Summary Report PDF page 109 (report page 101), section 7.1.5 Conclusions

title: Fabric flame shrinks in length and width before it goes out
statement: At quenching, the fabric flame is reported to shrink in both length and width, and the flame goes out in a three-dimensional manner.
supporting_experiment: BASS and BASS-II fabric tests (Summary Report section 7.1)
locations: Summary Report PDF page 109 (report page 101), section 7.1.5 Conclusions

statement: When the section was written, the pyrolysis rate constants of the fabric were still being determined so that quantitative comparisons between model and experiment could be made.

title: Critical opposed-flow velocity for radiative extinction of thin PMMA does not depend on thickness and rises as O2 falls
statement: Space-based tests of thin PMMA in low-speed opposed flow determined a critical flow velocity below which steady flame spread cannot be sustained, for various fuel thicknesses and two O2 levels. Results from four fuel thicknesses indicate that the critical velocity does not depend on fuel thickness and that it increases when the O2 level is decreased. Table 2.1 of the report lists experimental critical velocities of 10 +/- 5 mm/s at 21 percent O2 and 30 +/- 5 mm/s at 16 percent O2 (thin PMMA, 1 atm). A two-dimensional computation is reported to confirm this finding.
supporting_experiment: BASS-II opposed-flow flame spread over thin PMMA (Summary Report section 2.2)
locations: Summary Report PDF page 36 (report page 28), Table 2.1 and section 2.2.8 Conclusions
limitations: The experimental uncertainty is large (+/- 5 mm/s) and only two O2 levels are listed. The investigators of this section, the thicknesses tested and the number of tests were not read in this app. Critical velocity is not a column of the app dataset. A publication on this topic is listed in the PSI-25 metadata; it was not read, so it is not counted as extra support.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team

title: Interpretation: a simple scale analysis explains why the critical velocity does not depend on fuel thickness
statement: A simplified scale analysis is reported to give a closed-form expression for the critical velocity in terms of surface emissivity, gas properties and the vaporization, ambient and flame temperatures. It is reported to show that, although the flame spread rate is inversely proportional to fuel thickness, the critical velocity does not depend on thickness. The report describes the agreement with experiment and computation as remarkable in its conclusions and as reasonable in the text next to Table 2.1.
supporting_experiment: BASS-II opposed-flow flame spread over thin PMMA (Summary Report section 2.2)
locations: Summary Report PDF page 36 (report page 28), Table 2.1 and section 2.2.8 Conclusions
limitations: Table 2.1 lists theory values of 7.5 mm/s at 21 percent O2 and 10 mm/s at 16 percent O2, against experimental values of 10 +/- 5 and 30 +/- 5 mm/s (computation: 15 and 35 mm/s). The theory value lies inside the experimental range at 21 percent but below it at 16 percent. The report itself cites uncertainties of the experiments, the simplified model and the scale analysis.
review_status: draft: ratings proposed by the assistant and not yet reviewed by the team
